note: The Attorney General recovers civil penalties. The Office of Emergency Services receives incident reports and internal-use summaries, reviews incident reports (§ 22757.13(d)) and may designate equivalent federal standards (§ 22757.13(h)); no penalty power is given to it.

passages.locator: SEC. 2, Bus. & Prof. Code § 22757.12(a), opening clause
passages.quote: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework
shall declare its intent to do so to the Office of Emergency Services.
including a system card or model card, shall be deemed in compliance with the applicable paragraph.

note: Requires a developer framework, which describes how the developer approaches incorporating national standards, international standards and industry-consensus best practices (§ 22757.12(a)(1)). A frontier developer that declares its intent to comply with § 22757.13 through a federal law, regulation or guidance document designated by the Office of Emergency Services is “deemed in compliance” with that section to the extent it meets it (§ 22757.13(i)(2)(A)). Publishing transparency-report contents in a system or model card is deemed compliance (§ 22757.12(c)(3)). § 22757.12(c)(4) encourages disclosures consistent with industry best practices.

passages.quote: Before deploying a frontier model, the large developer of such frontier model shall do all of the following: (a) Implement a written safety and security protocol

note: “Safety and security protocol” is defined in § 1420(12) (p. 3) as documented technical and organizational protocols describing protections against critical harm, cybersecurity protections, a testing procedure, compliance and senior responsible personnel. § 1421(3) requires an annual review.

passages.quote: Conspicuously publish a copy of the safety and security protocol with appropriate redactions
transmit a copy of such redacted safety and security protocol to the attorney general and division of homeland security and emergency services

note: Before deploying a frontier model. Publication with “appropriate redactions” (defined in § 1420(1)) and transmission of the redacted copy to the attorney general and the division of homeland security and emergency services; § 1421(1)(c)(ii) adds access upon request (see Q06). Material modifications after annual review are published in the same manner (§ 1421(3)).

passages.quote: Before deploying a frontier model, the large developer of such frontier model shall do all of the following: (a) Implement a written safety and security protocol
industry best practices

note: Requires a developer’s written safety and security protocol. The annual review accounts for changes to model capabilities “and industry best practices” (§ 1421(3)). No code of practice or standard is named as a means of compliance, and no deemed-compliance provision was found.

note: Two defined terms bear the duties: “frontier developer” (transparency report, incident reporting, statements) and “large frontier developer” (framework, internal-use summaries, disclosure statement under § 1428, penalties under § 1427). § 1426 excludes accredited colleges and universities engaged in academic research and the Empire AI consortium. Ellipses in quotes from this record skip omitted words or the printed line numbers.

passages.locator: Bill text, § 2 (GBL § 1422(3)(a) as re-added), p. 6, lines 9–10
passages.quote: shall report any critical safety incident … to the office within seventy-two hours

note: Applies to all frontier developers. Seventy-two hours from a determination that an incident occurred or from learning facts sufficient for a reasonable belief that it occurred, to the office; twenty-four hours to an appropriate authority, including law enforcement or public safety agencies, where the incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury. Compliance through a designated federal standard is deemed compliance (§ 1422(9), see Q15).

statement: No UK law or other binding instrument placing duties on developers of frontier or general-purpose AI models was located. The 2024 King's Speech said the government would seek such legislation; the 2026 briefing notes contain none of the searched terms; the memoranda with developers state that they are not legally binding; and title searches of legislation.gov.uk for 2023–2026 found one instrument with "artificial intelligence" in its title, which places a duty on the Information Commissioner, not on developers.
